Confidence still prevails that an early solution will be found to post-strike problems arising at Canton but rumours prevail which tend to confuse the situation.
Cout优iielly, a denial has been made that seamen who were employed on certain Hong Kong river boats in June, 1925, have been reinstated at the cost of dismiss.

label: text
text: Then, again, a report is current that striking seamen have not been taken on yet but will be given positions on Monday, the first of the month.

label: text
text: Another disquieting rumour is that the Severance of Economic Relations Association will function as from Monday.

label: text
text: As a sequel, native merchants in Hong Kong are rushing up manufactured goods before the "embargo" comes into force.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: On the other hand, there is faith in the ability of piecegoods and metals dealers in Canton to hold out for a "no time limit" for clearance and disposal of British goods.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text:
No immediate relief is apparent in the picketing of the Steamboat Co.'s wharves at Canton.
As reported in yesterday's "China Mail," the British Consult General made representations to Mr. Eugene Cran who communicated with the Police Commissioner.

label: text
text: The sequel is the posting of detachments of armed police at the wharves but the plain clothes pickets have not withdrawn.

label: text
text: A report which came down yesterday predicts that the Canton police will have matters in hand within a few days, the interval being needed for the "peaceful" measures" to take their course.

label: text
text: Search Opposed.

label: text
text: It is expected that the authorities in Canton will communicate direct with the Strike Committee with regard to calling off the alleged ex-seamen and/or pickets from the Bund and wharves.

label: text

label: text

label: text
text: Allies Counter-Attack on

label: text
text: WU PEI-FU " SERIOUS."

label: text
text: Cantonese Losing Grip on

label: text
text: [By Our Special Correspondent.]

label: text
text: Old ground is being covered by the Northern Allies under Marshal Sun Chuan-fang. "In their latest counter-attack from Kiangxi, against Hupeh, along the course of the Yangtse River. Previously the Allies had reach a position, as the result of a prolonged and determined offensive; but they fell back suddenly when Chang Kai-shek struck at them in another direction. Since the lull—and as three Southern onslaughts on the Kiukiang-Nanchang line have failed—Sun Chuan-fang has been moving his men onwards again. Activities are, however, confined to his right wing.

label: text
text: Japanese reports on this front predict that the Cantonese may have to retire clean out of Kiangsi, as they are unable to exert further pressure.

label: text
text: That Nationalist headquarters does not anticipate much danger from Wu Pei-fu is evident from their transfer of Major-General Chan Ming-shu's famous division of "Iron troops" (from the 4th Army), from Hankow to the Kiangsi front.

label: text
text: But Wu Pei-fu insists that he is serious. Latest reports make out that he is still moving down slowly from the North but has not crossed the Hupeh frontier to any extent.

label: text
text: There has been no news from the interior of Kiangsi for more than a week. To the west of the Allied base at Nanchang, the Southerners are believed to be holding their ground, in close proximity to the Northern camp, with neither side wishing to call off the unofficial local truce.

label: text
text: The situation in Szechuan province continues to worsen. Attempts are being made to intimidate all employees of foreigners, and the boycott is now not only anti-British but anti-foreign; and is extending.

label: text
text: There have also been outbursts of anti-foreign feeling and it is feared it will be necessary to evacuate all British from Chengtu and places in the interior of the province shortly, in view of the inability of foreign warcraft to proceed up-river further than Chungking.—Reuter.
